correctness.rationale: For any a>0 and b real, direct Cartesian-to-polar computation gives radial derivative r^3(-a+b cos 2theta) and angular derivative r^2. The unique positive pi-periodic solution Q of Q'=1+(-2a+2b cos 2theta)Q is expressed by a convergent integral; its reciprocal integral over a half-turn is exactly 2 pi a. With C=Q(theta0)/r0^2, S=(t+C)r^2-Q(theta(t)) has zero initial condition and satisfies S'=2r^2(-a+b cos 2theta)S, hence vanishes identically. Its transformed phase yields a globally defined exact periodic log-time identity. If b is nonzero, the forcing cos 2theta recovered from Q forces least angular period pi, hence least log period 2 pi a. A nonconstant periodic quotient has no limit under a nonperiodic shift, proving the iff scaling group. Exact return times and the uniform b-small expansion follow. A checker tests 441 exact rational identities and representative integral/time identities but the proof is analytic. Assumptions include all nonzero initial conditions and exclude the origin from polar claims.

value.rationale: A globally attracting homogeneous cubic flow naturally prompts whether the leading inverse-time squared-radius decay coefficient exists. The result gives a strict necessary-and-sufficient boundary at zero anisotropy, a universal nonconstant exact profile at every nonzero anisotropy, a sharp multiplicative lattice of valid scaling ratios, a complete set of radial cluster values, and exact geometric physical-time return clocks for every nonzero trajectory. It therefore distinguishes stability from regular variation and supplies a reproducible temporal observable for a prominent non-polynomial Lyapunov example. The two-parameter family and all-scale iff statement avoid arbitrary parameter slicing, and the theorem does not misidentify a generic homogeneous scaling law as new.
